result.title: Fig: Automated Multiagent Behavior Elicitor
result.summary: Many social evaluations for multiagent systems study behaviors as they emerge from environments instead of systematically intervening in the environment to elicit such behaviors. We introduce Fig (Finding Interactions in Games), an agentic system that performs targeted elicitation interventions on game environments. It takes a natural language behavior description, decomposes it into sub-behaviors, generates new social games or selects existing ones, and executes single or combined interventions to the games' engine, opponents, instructions, and context. To evaluate model behavior, it combines built-in mechanical checks and synthetic rubric judgments. We validate the interventions, generated games, and evaluation mechanisms via human review. Models attempt the target behavior in 45.2% of episodes on average for valid scenarios generated by Fig for six test behaviors -- cooperation, exploitation, deception, covert coordination, betrayal, and sabotage. For game-behavior pairs with available controls, Fig's interventions increase attempt rates by 10.9% on average compared to matched control games. Fig shows that multiagent environments can serve as programmable test beds for intentional, controllable, and reproducible behavior evaluation. Code is available at https://github.com/fleet-ai/fig.

AI.brief_summary: Fig 是一个 agentic 系统：把自然语言描述的行为拆成子行为，自动生成或挑选社交游戏，并向游戏引擎、对手、指令与上下文施加单项或组合干预来诱发目标行为，再用内建机械检查与合成 rubric 评分进行评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「定向干预诱发行为＋子行为分解＋机械检查与 rubric 混合评判」思路可能可供核查：能否借助受控干预与自动评分检验 VLM 内部 latent 内容是否被因果使用，以及推理轨迹评价协议是否可靠。
